title: installer: add `upgrade plan` command (step graph) + version compatibility validation
author: Devon Price
release_notes: Private installer: new `upgrade plan` subcommand outputs an ordered step graph and validates version compatibility before applying upgrades.
body: Summary: This PR adds a new `upgrade plan` command to the Redwood Private installer. The command computes an upgrade plan without applying it, prints an ordered step graph (with component boundaries and gating checks), and validates version compatibility between the current deployment and the target bundle/chart versions. This is intended to be the first operator-visible piece of the Private upgrade/rollback project ("plan" before "apply"). Motivation: Operators and Support need a deterministic preview of what will change and a clear failure mode when a target version is incompatible (schema forward-only migrations, unsupported version skew, etc.). Today, upgrades fail late (during apply) with mixed logs across Helm/K8s; this command provides early, actionable feedback and a stable artifact (JSON output) for Support ingestion. What’s included: (1) `redwood-private upgrade plan` subcommand with two output modes: human-readable tree/graph and `--json` for machine parsing; (2) Plan builder that produces a DAG-ish structure (linearized for now) with explicit gates: "prechecks", "backup", "control-plane", "runtime", "gateway", "observability", "post-smoke"; (3) Version compatibility validation: fetch current component versions from control plane (when reachable) or fall back to installer state file; compare against target versions in bundle/helm chart metadata; fail fast with explicit remediation; (4) Docs updates: README + `docs/private-upgrades.md` describing plan usage, examples, and common failures; (5) Unit tests covering: parsing target versions, compatibility matrix evaluation, graph rendering, and JSON schema stability. UX notes: `upgrade plan` is non-destructive and safe to run repeatedly. It exits non-zero on incompatible targets and prints a short summary plus a `--verbose` section showing each rule evaluated. Example output (abbrev): `Plan: 9 steps (estimated downtime: 3-8m). 1) Prechecks (cluster/k8s/storage) 2) Backup (control-plane db snapshot) 3) Upgrade control plane (chart redwood-control-plane 1.16.0 -> 1.17.0) 4) Run migrations (gate: reversible=false) 5) Upgrade runtime (engine 0.9.3 -> 0.9.5) ...` Compatibility rules implemented (v1): (a) Control plane must be upgraded before gateway/runtime; (b) gateway version must be within [cp-1, cp+0] minor; (c) forward-only migrations block rollback; `upgrade plan` surfaces this as `rollback_supported=false` and prints a warning; (d) Helm chart major changes require explicit `--allow-major` (plan prints "blocked" step until flag is provided). Follow-ups: This PR does not implement `upgrade apply` or rollback; it focuses on plan/preview and early validation. Precheck runner and backup primitives land in separate PRs (ENG-2316/2317).
commits: cli: add `upgrade plan` command skeleton + help/flags
planner: implement step graph model + renderers (text + json)
compat: add version fetcher + compatibility rule engine
docs: add upgrade plan usage + examples
tests: unit tests for plan builder and compatibility validation
conversation: Connor O'Brien (review): The overall structure looks good. Two requests: (1) ensure the plan output is stable across runs (sorting), and (2) the compatibility failure needs to include the exact skew rule that failed (copy/pasteable for Support).
Devon Price (author): Done. Graph nodes are now sorted by `phase_order` then `component`. Compatibility errors now include `rule_id` + a one-line remediation hint.

Quentin Harris (review): On compatibility: can we make the matrix data-driven? Hardcoding rules in code is okay for v1, but I'd like a clear seam for reading from bundle metadata later. Also, please confirm how we handle "control plane unreachable" during plan.

Devon Price (author): Added an interface `CompatibilitySource` with a default in-code implementation. Bundle-metadata source can be added later without touching CLI. For control plane unreachable: we try API first; on failure we fall back to installer state file and mark `source=statefile` in JSON output plus a warning in text output.

Ethan Park (review): The fallback is fine, but please make the warning explicit that version detection is partial and might be wrong if state drifted. Also, can you include the control plane endpoint you attempted (redacted/normalized) for troubleshooting?
Devon Price (author): Updated warning copy and added `control_plane_endpoint_hint` (scheme+host only) to JSON; text output prints `cp endpoint: https://<host>` if available.

Kenji Nakamura (review): Text output: the "graph" is readable, but the indentation makes it look like nested steps. Can we label gates explicitly (e.g. `[gate]`) and steps as `[step]` so Support screenshots are unambiguous?
Devon Price (author): Implemented `[step]` and `[gate]` prefixes and aligned indentation. Also added `--format=graph|table|json` (default graph) so people can copy/paste a compact table into tickets.
Rafael Mendes (review): Please add a doc snippet showing how SRE should use this in a change window (plan, save JSON, attach to ticket).
Devon Price (author): Added a short runbook-style section in `docs/private-upgrades.md` with command examples and a recommended artifact (`upgrade-plan.json`).
Connor O'Brien (approval): LGTM. This unblocks prechecks/backup PRs. Please follow up with a small PR to wire `upgrade plan --json` into diagnostics bundle once that lands.
Quentin Harris (approval): Approved. Thanks for adding the compatibility seam.
